title: Trust, efficient contracting and export upgrading
summary: Research on contracting institutions and export quality has largely overlooked informal institutions. The paper tests whether trust drives product-quality upgrading by easing contractual frictions, and finds that contract-intensive industries in high-trust countries upgrade more.
keyFindings: Contract-intensive industries in high-trust societies see a disproportionately larger rise in producing and exporting higher-quality products.
The result holds after controlling for conventional sources of comparative advantage and formal institutions.
Strong informal institutions can support market performance even where formal institutions are weak.
methods: Industry-level data for 1995–2014, estimated with a generalised difference-in-differences design.
